research_question: Define cloud computing, service and deployment models
findings: Defines 5 essential characteristics, 3 service models (SaaS/PaaS/IaaS), 4 deployment models; hybrid cloud = composition of two or more distinct infrastructures bound by technology enabling data and application portability
limitations: Definitional; no performance or portability evidence
relevance: Vocabulary for local/private vs public and hybrid; the term 'hybrid' in SETU-X follows this definition

research_question: What cloud computing is and its obstacles/opportunities
findings: Discusses the potential of and obstacles to cloud computing (abstract only read in this review)
limitations: Full text not accessible here; used only for general context
relevance: Background context only; no specific claim relies on it

research_question: How Google manages large clusters with Borg
findings: Borg runs hundreds of thousands of jobs from thousands of applications across clusters of up to tens of thousands of machines
relevance: Lineage of container orchestration ideas behind Kubernetes and Compose-style declarative deployment

research_question: Lessons from Borg, Omega, Kubernetes
findings: Containers as unit of management (application-oriented infrastructure); pods; labels; /healthz health checks enable automatic restart (self-healing)
relevance: Justifies per-service health endpoints, container-as-unit design, labels for environment placement
read_depth: full text (ACM Queue version of the same article)

research_question: Why latency variability matters at scale and how to tolerate it
findings: Fan-out magnifies component variability (e.g., 1-in-100 slow server and 100-way fan-out -> 63% of requests slow); hedged/tied requests reduce tail latency; naive hedging adds load
limitations: Google-scale; techniques assume replicas and spare capacity
relevance: Basis for H1 (critical path / fan-out) and H5 (retries add load); report tail percentiles not just means

research_question: Microservice implications across the stack
metrics: tail latency, throughput, network processing share
findings: Network processing is a large share of execution (e.g., 36.3% for Social Network); one mismanaged dependency raised tail latency 10.4x; slow servers cause cascading QoS violations
limitations: Specific hardware; no dedicated limitations section
relevance: Motivates measuring per-dependency latency and failure propagation; context for H1/H2

research_question: Characterize microservice vs monolith workloads
findings: Microservice version up to 79.2% lower performance than monolith on same hardware; large runtime/library overhead
relevance: Microservice boundaries cost performance; our measured overhead column makes that visible

research_question: Characterize microservice dependency and performance in production
findings: Call graphs heavy-tailed, tree-like, many hotspot services; three types of call dependency; performance sensitive to CPU interference
relevance: Supports modelling the call graph explicitly (H4); our graph is deliberately tiny

research_question: Typical faults and debugging practice in microservices
methodology: Survey plus benchmark plus empirical study
findings: Existing industrial debugging practice can be improved with tracing and visualization
relevance: Supports request correlation IDs and per-dependency latency capture

research_question: Predictability of performance in public IaaS clouds
methodology: Literature review (15 hypotheses) plus large experiments
findings: Substantial differences between providers; multitenancy has dramatic impact for some providers
relevance: Why local results cannot stand in for provider performance; provider comparison needs real repeated measurements

research_question: Performance variability of production cloud services
findings: About half of services show yearly and daily patterns; also periods of stable performance
relevance: Time-of-day effects are a threat to validity for any real-cloud run; record timestamps

research_question: Variance of runtime measurements on EC2
findings: EC2 performance varies a lot and often falls into two bands
relevance: Supports repeated runs and reporting spread; local cluster baseline was more stable

research_question: Reproducibility of big-data performance in cloud networks
findings: Network variability persists and can be exacerbated by QoS mechanisms; research often ignores variability
relevance: Key reason our fixed injected delay is a simplification of real networks

research_question: Client-to-cloud latency across major providers
findings: Current cloud coverage can support several latency-critical applications
relevance: Source of realistic magnitudes to motivate (not calibrate) delay ranges; real-cloud path should measure instead

research_question: How to measure and report cloud performance
findings: Eight principles: repeated experiments, workload/config coverage, setup description, open artifact, probabilistic result description, statistical evaluation, units, cost
relevance: Directly shapes our methodology: repeats, full distributions, units, artifacts, cost modelling

research_question: Statistically sound benchmarking and reporting
findings: State of practice lacking; proposes statistically sound analysis and reporting rules
relevance: Supports CIs, nonparametric summaries, and explicit reporting rules

research_question: Is performance testing of microservices stable?
workload: TeaStore at 700-900 req/s, 10 reps x 18 scenarios
findings: Environments and response times unstable across runs; single runs flaky for regression detection; 10 runs reliable
relevance: Run is the unit of replication; need multiple runs before claiming a difference

research_question: Reference microservice app for research
findings: Provides services with different performance characteristics for benchmarking and modelling
limitations: Reference app, not an experiment harness
relevance: Alternative system under test; we choose a smaller app for laptop-scale clarity

research_question: Principles of chaos engineering
findings: Experimentation verifies reliability of complex distributed systems
relevance: Frames our bounded, hypothesis-driven fault experiments

research_question: Systematic resilience testing of microservices
methodology: Framework that manipulates inter-service messages at network layer
findings: Found previously unknown failure-handling bugs without modifying the application
relevance: Prior work on message-level fault injection; we inject at the client library instead

research_question: Service-level fault injection testing (Filibuster)
methodology: Instrumented HTTP clients plus systematic exploration
findings: Found all corpus bugs (e.g., misconfigured timeouts, fallback to same server) before production
relevance: Closest technique to ours (client-level injection); our focus is measurement rather than test generation; motivates H2/H3

research_question: Deployment strategies for circuit breaker, discovery, gateway
findings: Insights on where to place circuit breakers
relevance: Design reference for our breaker placement in the caller

research_question: Large-scale distributed tracing
findings: Low-overhead sampled tracing via instrumentation of common libraries
relevance: Rationale for propagating request/trace IDs across services

research_question: Does NetEm behave as specified?
findings: Delay and uncorrelated loss conform; realized jitter lower than configured
relevance: Even kernel emulation deviates; our app-level delay must be validated and labelled

research_question: Scalability of network emulation in virtual edge testbeds
findings: NetEm imposes prohibitive scalability limits; proposes eBPF-based way forward
relevance: Supports our choice not to rely on netem (also needs NET_ADMIN) and to document emulation limits

research_question: VM vs container performance
environment: KVM vs Docker on one host
findings: Containers equal or better than VMs in almost all cases; both need tuning for I/O
relevance: Container overhead is low but not zero; local Docker networking is not cloud networking

research_question: History and open problems of microservices
findings: Reviews evolution to microservices and open challenges
relevance: Background on microservice style

research_question: State of multi-cloud and requirements
findings: Technological and administrative barriers slow multi-cloud; lists basic requirements
relevance: Motivates provider-neutral adapter interface

research_question: Inter-cloud architectures and brokering taxonomy
findings: Inter-cloud aims at better QoS, reliability, cost; field immature; open challenges
relevance: Motivates explicit placement/brokering decisions and their reasons

research_question: Vendor lock-in risk from a business perspective
findings: Lock-in exacerbated as resources move to cloud; interoperability and portability matter
relevance: Motivates portability; reminds us multi-cloud is not automatically beneficial

research_question: QoS-aware deployment across fog/cloud
methodology: Model plus algorithms plus FogTorch prototype
findings: Determines eligible deployments from latency/bandwidth model
relevance: Placement as a function of link latency; we measure instead of only modelling (H4)

research_question: App-based vs service-based microservice placement
findings: Service-based strategies outperformed or equalled app-based
relevance: Example of simulation-only placement evidence; contrasts with running containers
